messages:
maria: Quick update from this morning's bring-up of Liminal12B v2 across quant profiles. Posting high-level perf, quality, and an ops/GTM rec.
leo: great — short summary first?
maria: perf summary (p4d, concurrent=16): single-token p95: fp16 ~ 26ms, int8 ~ 32ms, int4 ~ 48ms. Throughput (tokens/sec): fp16 720, int8 920, int4 1400.
owen: throughput delta is huge for int4. quality numbers?
maria: ran three slices (short chat, abstractive summarization, multi-turn long QA). Relative to fp16 baseline: int8 aggregated EM -1.1%, ROUGE -0.9; int4 EM -4.6%, ROUGE -3.8. Main int4 failure modes: entity swaps in multi-turn, occasional hallucinated dates, and truncated tails on 1.5k+ summaries.
ashley: product: would we consider int4 for any production surface? Sounds risky for summarization.
maria: recommendation: int8 as the standard production profile. Int4 only as an opt-in low-risk cost tier or burst path. But hybrid routing can unlock most cost upside without large quality regressions.
leo: what's the tail latency story? p99s?
maria: p99 single-token: fp16 70ms, int8 110ms, int4 220ms. Observed spikes when sequences exceed 4096 tokens due to kernel fallback and additional memcpy. Also cold-start kv-cache on int4 showed 4x slower first few tokens until warm cache.
owen: can we classify "complex" requests to keep them on fp16?
maria: yes. Proposed complexity classifier rules: prompt length > 1024 tokens OR named-entity ratio > 0.12 OR conversation depth > 4 OR presence of code blocks. Complex -> fp16. Default -> int8. Int4 only for short one-shot prompts with low entity density.
ashley: unit-econ numbers for GTN? customers will ask.
maria: infra-only token cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.025, int8 $0.017, int4 $0.010. Example traffic mix (50% short chat, 30% summarization, 20% long QA). Simulated monthly cost for 20M tokens: fp16 $500, int8 $340, int4 $200. Hybrid (int8 + fp16 for complex) ~ $360.
leo: how much quality do we lose under hybrid?
maria: hybrid keeps EM loss ~ -0.9% aggregated vs fp16; summarization ROUGE loss ~ -0.7 because long summaries are pinned to fp16.
ashley: what's an acceptable GTN message?
maria: Draft: "Liminal12B v2 — recommended: int8 for production workloads; int4 for experimental cost-saving bursts. Use our hybrid routing recipe to maintain fidelity on complex prompts while cutting unit cost ~30% vs fp16."
owen: ops risks? memory, warmup, monitoring needs?
maria: ops notes: 1) cold kv warmup penalty for int4 (mitigate with prefill of 32 tokens on session start), 2) kernel fallback beyond 4096 triggers memcpy spikes, 3) observed sporadic CUDA mem thrashing on long mixed workloads with int4 quantized-ops (increase reserved headroom), 4) ensure tracing includes kernel id and sequence length for easier triage.
leo: rollout plan? canary thresholds?
maria: propose canary: 3 stage rollout (2% -> 15% -> 60%) for int8 default + complexity routing. Capture fidelity signals and sample top-100 failure cases per slice after 24h. Terminate if any slice EM drops > 0.8% or P99 latency regression > 50% for 24h.
ashley: GTN deliverable: one-page scorecard + routing recipe + sample email for customers. We'll label int4 as "experimental" with explicit caveats.
bench-bot: Perf artifacts uploaded -> s3://bench-reports/liminal12b-v2/3419991111/; full logs + per-kernel timings + per-slice eval.csv.
maria: actionable recs (short):
1) Default config: int8 with quant-kv cache enabled and prefill=32.
2) Complexity classifier -> fp16 for complex prompts.
3) Int4: enable only as opt-in burst pool in Dedicated; do not enable by default in Hosted.
4) Canary recipe: 2%->15%->60%, fidelity checks at each stage, rollback on per-slice EM >0.8%.
5) Ops: add kernel fallback + seq-length based alert, reserve +15% GPU memory headroom for int4 runs.
6) Docs: publish a succinct scorecard (perf numbers, quality deltas, routing recipe, known failure modes).
leo: I'll file the canary automation ticket and add alerts for kernel-fallback signatures.
owen: I'll take ops risk mitigation (prefill + memory headroom).
nashley: I'll draft GTN blurb and customer-facing note.
maria: thanks all 44d I'll upload the runbook and link the artifacts.
bench-bot: CI snapshot: smoke + perf checks passed; extended eval queued (ETA ~8h).
